newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB joins forces with Swiss Bank to brave reforms.
newsitem.headline: LTCB joins forces with Swiss Bank to brave reforms.

text.p: Another Japanese bank on Tuesday said it would join forces with a foreign counterpart to brave Tokyo's "Big Bang" financial reforms -- this time the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB).
The leading Japanese long-term credit bank said it would form a strategic alliance with Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), one of the largest banking groups in the world.
The pillars of the tie-up would be joint ventures based in Japan covering investment banking, asset management and private banking, the two banks said.
"This strategy realises one objective -- to take Japan to the world, and bring the world to Japan," LTCB president Katsunobu Onogi told reporters.
"Our alliance with SBC is the perfect response to the opportunities presented by the Big Bang," he said.
To cement the ties, each bank will purchase a three percent equity stake in the other.

"We know that together we can deliver on our shared objective because we will be home to the most creative, dynamic and client-focussed team in the world," Johannes De Gier, SBC Warburg executive chairman, told the news conference.

LTCB, which was founded in 1952, said that subject to board approval, it was considering raising about 200 billion yen ($1.8 billion) in capital through issuing preferred stock, bringing the bank's international capital adequacy ratio to 11 or 12 percent.
SBC Warburg Securities will help LTCB raise those funds by holding about 50 percent of the new LTCB preferred stock in its investment portfolio, the banks said.
They said that in the investment banking sphere, they were planning to form a jointly managed partnership, called LTCB SBC Warburg Securities, capitalised at 60 billion yen($522 million).

The partnership, which is expected to commence in early 1998, will be responsible for the Japanese investment banking business of both firms, combining LTCB Securities and SBC Warburg's operations in Japan.

LTCB and SBC will also set up an asset management firm, LTCB SBC Brinson, and a private banking concern, which will be Japan's first-ever private bank, to "maximise the opportunities afforded by the $10.5 trillion in financial assets held by Japanese individuals", the banks said.
The alliance of LTCB and SBC -- which have assets of more than $266 billion -- is the third in a series of similar unions between sickly Japanese banks and robust foreign counterparts.

In June, ailing Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd said that it will work together with Britain's Barclays Bank in such areas as the development of new financial products and the securitisation of assets held by Hokkaido Takushoku.

This followed a similar announcement by troubled Nippon Credit Bank Ltd and Bankers Trust New York Corp. Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters shortly after the announcement that the alliances was likely to boost confidence in LTCB and more tie-ups were expected due to the "Big Bang" reforms, which are designed to liberate Japan's financial markets.
"It is up to management's judgment to form alliances, but I think such moves are likely to become a trend in the future," Mitsuzuka said. ($1=114 yen)
